mainTopic: Hanging walls (מחיצה תלויה) for סוכה, עירובין and שבת, and using לבוד to build a valid סוכה wall
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה in עירובין about a cistern shared by two courtyards. רבי יהודה says the courtyard wall hanging over the water is enough. רבי יוחנן links this to רבי יוסי, who says a hanging wall (מחיצה תלויה) works for סוכה. The גמרא rejects the link: רבי יהודה is lenient only for עירובי חצירות, which is דרבנן, and רבי יוסי is lenient only for סוכה, not for the severe laws of שבת. The ציפורי incident, where people carried a ספר תורה on שבת using sheets already hanging on posts, followed a third view, רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי. Next, אבימי teaches that a mat of four טפחים and a bit can be a סוכה wall by using לבוד twice, above and below. A ברייתא requiring seven טפחים is explained as a tall סוכה, where the wall hangs down from above like רבי יוסי. Finally, רבי אמי's board placed near a wall teaches that a small סוכה must be seven טפחים long.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree on where the cistern partition goes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה about a cistern between two courtyards. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree on where the partition must be placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: from above. בית הלל say: from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה in עירובין. It is setting up the source it will compare to our סוכה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a cistern shared by two courtyards, with no עירוב between them. To draw water on שבת, the cistern must be divided by a partition. One opinion requires the partition above the water and the other below, at the water itself. Either way, both agree some special partition is needed for the cistern.
steps.confusionAlert: The Hebrew text quoted here says בית שמאי require it 'above' and בית הלל 'below'. The משנה in עירובין, and Sefaria's English translation of this line, have the reverse: בית שמאי say below, בית הלל say above. The point that matters for our סוכה סוגיא does not change. Both sides require a special partition for the cistern, and רבי יהודה (next step) disagrees with that.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: from above,
phrases.notes: In the משנה in עירובין, this word is מִלְּמַטָּה instead.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: from below.
phrases.notes: In the משנה in עירובין, this word is מִלְמַעְלָה instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה in עירובין that earlier began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a special partition for a shared cistern. They disagree only on whether it goes above or below.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the courtyard wall is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says no special cistern partition is needed. The wall dividing the two courtyards already counts, even though it only hangs above the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: A partition should not be stricter than the wall that is between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a third opinion. The existing courtyard wall, which runs across the top of the cistern, already divides the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard wall does not reach down into the water. It only 'hangs' over it. By saying it is enough, רבי יהודה is accepting a hanging wall as a real partition. This is what the גמרא will compare to סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Wall (here, the wall between the courtyards)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source the גמרא will try to link to רבי יוסי's view that a hanging wall works for סוכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
a partition should not be greater (stricter)
than the wall that is between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא תְּהֵא מְחִיצָה גְּדוֹלָה מִן הַכּוֹתֶל שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יהודה's dissenting opinion within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The existing courtyard wall above the cistern is a sufficient partition. This means a hanging partition works.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן links רבי יהודה to רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. He says רבי יהודה's view follows the opinion of רבי יוסי, who holds that a hanging wall is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה said it following the approach of רבי יוסי, who said a hanging partition permits.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא connects two opinions. רבי יהודה's cistern rule rests on the same idea as רבי יוסי's view on סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי (in our פרק) allows a hanging wall for סוכה. רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה's ruling in עירובין uses the same principle, מחיצה תלויה מתרת. That would make them one shared view across both areas of halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging partition, one that does not reach the ground

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda stated it in line with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei,
who said that a hanging partition permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view by linking it to רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי share one principle: a hanging partition is valid.

steps.title: The גמרא denies the two opinions are the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי יוחנן's link. Neither רבי יהודה holds like רבי יוסי, nor does רבי יוסי hold like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the linkage. It states a two-part claim, which it will now explain one part at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim works in both directions. רבי יהודה's view does not imply רבי יוסי's view, and רבי יוסי's view does not imply רבי יהודה's. This line is a heading for the explanations that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (a rejection formula)

steps.confusionAlert: Each רבי still holds his own ruling. What the גמרא rejects is only the claim that both rulings rest on one shared principle.

phrases.english: But that is not so;

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: neither does Rabbi Yehuda hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: nor does Rabbi Yosei hold like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the equation proposed in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי share one principle about hanging partitions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each view has its own limits, so neither one implies the other. The details are explained in the next steps.

steps.title: רבי יהודה is lenient only for a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה accepts a hanging wall only for עירובי חצירות, which is דרבנן. For סוכה, which is דאורייתא, he would not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה only said it there, about joining courtyards, which is rabbinic. But here, סוכה is from the Torah, so no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of its rejection. It shows why רבי יהודה's leniency does not carry over to סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbinic laws allow more leniency than Torah laws. רבי יהודה may accept a hanging wall for a rabbinic matter like עירובי חצירות. That does not mean he would accept it for סוכה, a Torah מצוה. So רבי יוסי's leniency for סוכה goes further than anything רבי יהודה said.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said it up to this point (limits a statement to its own case)
Joining courtyards so one may carry between them on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: A leniency given in a דרבנן area cannot automatically be applied to a דאורייתא area like סוכה. So רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move across ש״ס: separating a דרבנן leniency from a דאורייתא case to break an apparent link between two opinions.

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said it there,
regarding the joining of courtyards, which is rabbinic.
But here, with a sukka, which is from the Torah, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the two-part rejection in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Whether רבי יהודה's leniency can be applied to סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The link ignores the difference between a דרבנן area (עירובי חצירות) and a דאורייתא area (סוכה).

steps.title: רבי יוסי accepts a hanging wall for סוכה but not for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting רבי יוחנן's link. רבי יוסי accepts a hanging wall only for סוכה, which is a positive commandment. He does not accept it for שבת, where the penalty is סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי יהודה either. רבי יוסי only said a hanging wall works here, for a סוכה, which is a positive commandment. But for שבת, where the sin is punished by stoning, he would not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second half of its rejection from Step 4. It shows that רבי יוסי also would not agree with רבי יהודה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that רבי יהודה is lenient only in a דרבנן area. Now we see that רבי יוסי is lenient only for a positive commandment like סוכה. Carrying on שבת is a severe prohibition punished by סקילה, so there he would be strict. Each one is lenient in a different place, so neither can be used as a source for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition whose penalty is death by stoning
'He only said it up to here', meaning the ruling is limited to this case
Holds like, agrees with the view of

steps.confusionAlert: סוכה is still a Torah-level מצוה. The point is not that סוכה is דרבנן. A positive commandment is simply less severe than a prohibition punished by סקילה, so רבי יוסי allows the leniency only there.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה accepts a hanging wall only for עירובי חצירות, which is דרבנן. רבי יוסי accepts it only for סוכה, a positive commandment. Their leniencies do not overlap, so רבי יוחנן's link is rejected from both directions.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only stated his view here,
regarding a sukkah, which is a positive commandment.
But Shabbat, which is a prohibition punished by stoning, no.
phrases.notes: For שבת, a hanging wall would not work according to רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided rejection begun in Steps 4 and 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יוסי would agree with רבי יהודה's hanging wall in a שבת-related case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's leniency is limited to a positive commandment and does not reach a severe סקילה prohibition

steps.title: Whose opinion did the ציפורי incident follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a question. If רבי יוסי does not accept hanging walls for שבת, whose view did the incident in ציפורי follow? There they relied on hanging walls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the incident that happened in ציפורי, whose opinion was it done by?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty. A known incident relied on a hanging wall on שבת, and it seemed to follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just said that רבי יוסי would not accept a hanging wall for שבת. But people apparently thought the ציפורי incident followed רבי יוסי, which would contradict Step 6. So the גמרא must explain whose authority that incident rested on.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say', introducing a possible objection
An incident or actual event, often used as precedent
ציפורי, a city in the גליל
On whose authority, or according to whom

phrases.english: And if you will say: the incident that took place in Tzippori,
according to whose ruling was it done?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit just placed on רבי יוסי's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that רבי יוסי does not accept hanging walls for שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real precedent relied on hanging walls on שבת. If it followed רבי יוסי, then Step 6 is wrong.

steps.title: It followed רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The incident did not follow רבי יוסי. It followed his son, רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not done according to רבי יוסי. It was done according to רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty. It credits the ציפורי incident to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son held a broader leniency than his father. In his view, a hanging wall works even for שבת. So the incident does not contradict what we said about רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוסי, a תנא

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a third view. Unlike רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי accepts a hanging wall even for a Torah-level שבת prohibition.

phrases.english: Not according to Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: but rather according to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֶלָּא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the precedent to a different authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציפורי incident followed רבי יוסי, which would contradict his limit
steps.terutzMaskana: It followed רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי, who is lenient even for שבת

steps.title: What was the incident?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly happened in the ציפורי incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was the incident?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is preparing to tell the story of the incident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the incident was only mentioned by name. Now the גמרא asks for the details so we can see how a hanging wall was used on שבת.

phrases.english: And what was the incident?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the incident mentioned in Steps 7 and 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The facts of the ציפורי incident

steps.title: רב דימי tells the story of the forgotten Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports what happened. People forgot to bring a ספר תורה before שבת. They then hung sheets on posts to make walls and brought it through.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: Once they forgot and did not bring a ספר תורה before שבת. The next day they spread sheets over the posts, brought the ספר תורה, and read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting רב דימי's account of the incident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheets hung on top of the posts and did not reach the ground, so they were hanging walls. Relying on them for carrying on שבת is exactly the leniency of רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came, he said:
Once they forgot

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הֵבִיאוּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and did not bring a Torah scroll on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר פֵּירְסוּ סְדִינִין עַל גַּבֵּי הָעַמּוּדִים,
phrases.english: the next day they spread sheets over the posts,
and they brought a Torah scroll and read from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They hung sheets on posts as walls and carried the ספר תורה on שבת

steps.title: How could they spread sheets on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of the story. How could they bring sheets on שבת before the walls existed? That carrying itself would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think they spread the sheets? From where did they bring them on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to one detail in רב דימי's story. It says the story cannot be read literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had to carry the sheets out on שבת to make the walls, that carrying would happen before any walls were up. That would be forbidden. So 'they spread' cannot mean they hung the sheets on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Would it enter your mind?', meaning this cannot be right

phrases.english: Does it enter your mind that they spread them?
From where did they bring them on Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of רב דימי's report
steps.kashyaTarget: The word פֵּירְסוּ (they spread) in the story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing the sheets on שבת would itself be forbidden carrying, since there were no walls yet

steps.title: The sheets were already hanging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the story. They found sheets already spread on the posts, and they used them as walls to bring the ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they found sheets already spread over the posts, and they brought the ספר תורה and read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the story. The sheets were already in place before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the problem of carrying the sheets on שבת. The core point of the story stays the same: they relied on hanging walls for a שבת carrying issue. That fits רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי, not רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: The ציפורי incident relied on hanging walls on שבת. It follows a third view, רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי himself accepts hanging walls only for סוכה, and רבי יהודה only for עירובי חצירות.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מָצְאוּ סְדִינִין פְּרוּסִין עַל גַּבֵּי הָעַמּוּדִים
phrases.english: Rather, they found sheets spread over the posts
and they brought a Torah scroll and read from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of Step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They hung the sheets on שבת itself
steps.terutzMaskana: The sheets were already hanging, and they only relied on them as walls
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Relying on hanging walls for שבת follows רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוסי

steps.title: A mat just over four handbreadths can be a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes אבימי: a mat four טפחים and a bit wide can serve as a סוכה wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: A mat that is four handbreadths and a little more makes a סוכה kosher by serving as a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. A fairly small mat can count as a full wall of a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה wall must be ten טפחים high. Four and a bit is far short of that, so we will need an explanation of how such a small mat reaches the full height.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Avimi said:
A mat of four handbreadths and a bit
makes a sukkah permitted, as a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story from ציפורי ended in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mat four טפחים and a bit can serve as a valid סוכה wall.

steps.title: How does such a small mat work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a four-טפח mat can make a ten-טפח wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question. It sets up the next step, which explains how the mat is placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. The גמרא wants to know how to hang the mat so that it counts as ten טפחים.

phrases.english: How does he do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ruling in Step 13 works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a mat of four טפחים and a bit reaches the needed ten טפחים.

steps.title: Hang it in the middle and use לבוד twice
steps.stepSummary: The mat is hung with a gap of less than three טפחים below it and less than three above it. Each gap counts as closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He hangs it in the middle, with less than three handbreadths below it and less than three above it. Anything less than three handbreadths is treated as if it were joined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The mat hangs in the middle of the ten-טפח space, and both gaps are filled in by לבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four and a bit for the mat, plus almost three below, plus almost three above, adds up to ten. Each gap is under three טפחים, so the law treats it as closed. That makes the whole space one ten-טפח wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A gap of less than three טפחים that the law treats as closed

steps.confusionAlert: לבוד does not make the mat bigger. It treats the small empty gap as if it were solid, so the gap becomes part of the wall.

phrases.english: He hangs it in the middle,
less than three below
and less than three above,
and anything less than three is like joined (lavud).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mat hangs in the middle, and לבוד is applied both above and below it to reach ten טפחים.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אבימי needed to teach this, since לבוד is a well-known rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבימי's ruling as unnecessary. Everyone already knows the rule of לבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לבוד is an accepted rule, applying it here seems to add nothing new. The גמרא wants to know what new point אבימי is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling explained in Step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לבוד is already known, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The new point: לבוד can be used twice
steps.stepSummary: One might think לבוד can only be used once. אבימי teaches that it can be used twice, above and below.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we apply לבוד once, but we do not apply לבוד twice. So he teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling does teach something new. לבוד can be applied twice to the same wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using לבוד once is well known. Using it on two sides of one small mat might seem like stretching the rule too far. אבימי tells us this is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. A source that seems to need seven טפחים would imply that only one לבוד is allowed.

phrases.english: You might have said:
we say lavud once,
we do not say lavud twice —
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לבוד can be used only once.
steps.terutzMaskana: לבוד can be used twice, above and below.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the mat must be seven handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a mat of seven טפחים and a bit makes the סוכה kosher. That seems to allow only one לבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A mat of seven handbreadths and a bit makes a סוכה kosher as a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבימי from a ברייתא. The ברייתא requires a mat of seven and a bit, not four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven and a bit plus one gap of almost three adds up to ten. That uses לבוד only once. If two לבוד were allowed, the ברייתא should have said four.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A mat of seven and a bit
makes a sukkah permitted, as a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the double-לבוד rule from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבימי's four-טפח mat using two לבוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires seven and a bit, which fits only one לבוד. That suggests two לבוד are not allowed.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a tall סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of a large, tall סוכה, so it is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a large סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deals with a different case: a tall סוכה, not a ten-טפח one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a tall סוכה, the mat is hung near the top, within three טפחים of the סכך. It does not reach the ground at all. So the ברייתא is not about using לבוד twice, and it does not contradict אבימי.

phrases.english: When that one was taught,
it was about a large sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a different case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a ten-טפח סוכה and rules out two לבוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a tall סוכה, so אבימי's rule stands.

steps.title: So what is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the ברייתא makes if it is about a tall סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does it teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson the ברייתא holds once we read it as a tall-סוכה case. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is not about לבוד from the ground, it must be teaching something else. The גמרא wants to name that lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: And what does it teach us?

phrases.english: And what does it teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the new reading from Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lesson of the ברייתא once it is set in a tall סוכה.

steps.title: Walls can hang down from above, like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that a wall can hang down from the top, following רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That we may lower walls from above going down, like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא teaches about hanging walls. A wall that hangs from the top, without reaching the ground, can count, as רבי יוסי holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat hangs within three טפחים of the סכך and hangs in the air below. It still counts as a wall because of רבי יוסי's view that a hanging wall works. This ties back to the earlier discussion of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: אבימי's rule stands: לבוד can be used twice in a ten-טפח סוכה. The seven-טפח ברייתא is about a tall סוכה, where a wall hangs down from above as רבי יוסי holds.

phrases.english: that we lower walls
from above downward
in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 and closes the challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches that hanging walls are valid, following רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A board just over four handbreadths, placed near a wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that a board four טפחים and a bit can serve as a wall if it is placed less than three טפחים from an existing wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: A board of four handbreadths and a bit makes a סוכה kosher as a wall. He places it less than three handbreadths from the wall, and anything less than three handbreadths from the wall is treated as joined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling that uses לבוד. Here the gap is sideways, between a board and an existing wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The board stands with a gap of less than three טפחים between it and the existing wall. לבוד treats the gap as closed. So the board joins the wall and covers the full width needed for that side.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that לבוד works sideways too, closing a gap between a board and a wall, not only up and down.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
A board of four and a bit
makes a sukkah permitted, as a wall.
And he places it less than three handbreadths
near the wall,
and anything less than three near the wall
is like joined (lavud).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling that also uses לבוד, this time sideways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A board four טפחים and a bit, placed less than three טפחים from an existing wall, counts as a valid סוכה wall through לבוד.

steps.title: What new point is רבי אמי teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is new in רבי אמי's ruling, since the rule of לבוד is already known.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new idea רבי אמי's ruling adds. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone already knows that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed (לבוד). So saying a board under three טפחים from a wall works seems to teach nothing new. The גמרא wants to find the real lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what is new in a statement)
The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as if it were closed

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: The rule of לבוד is already known, so what is new here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what new idea is in the ruling of רבי אמי from Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new halachic point רבי אמי's ruling teaches beyond the known rule of לבוד.

steps.title: A small סוכה must be at least seven טפחים long
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that the minimum length of a small סוכה is seven טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: the minimum length of a small סוכה is seven טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי's real lesson is the size of a small סוכה. Its wall must reach a length of seven טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers in רבי אמי's ruling were chosen on purpose. A board of four טפחים and a bit, plus a gap of just under three (closed by לבוד), adds up to seven. That tells us seven טפחים is the length a small סוכה needs.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he teaches us (introduces the new point)
A small סוכה, the smallest kosher size

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's ruling is not about לבוד itself. It teaches that a small סוכה must be seven טפחים long, made up of four and a bit of board plus under three of gap.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lesson is the rule of לבוד. Everyone knows that. The new point is the number seven: the board plus the gap must add up to the length of a small סוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why רבי אמי used exactly four and a bit: that is the least board needed so that, with לבוד, the wall reaches seven טפחים.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
phrases.notes: Introduces the answer to the question.

phrases.english: the minimum length of a small sukkah
phrases.notes: The horizontal length of the wall.

phrases.english: is seven (handbreadths).
phrases.notes: A board of a little over four handbreadths, plus a gap of under three, adds up to seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 by showing what is new in רבי אמי's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling teaches that a small סוכה must be at least seven טפחים long, which the board (four and a bit) plus the לבוד gap (under three) reaches.
